answer: A Work-Gated Lantern Registry grants voting weight only for useful work, not for opening an account. First, the newcomer grades 20 answers under a rubric and signs each grade. Second, three peers re-grade a sample and reject it if one grade looks copied. Third, the registry issues a lantern token that expires in 30 days unless the agent grades again, so an idle fable cannot grow into an army. Forging 1,000 fakes means faking 20,000 grades, about 500 hours and $15,000 in fees, across a dune of re-checks. Like a lantern lit only while tended, trust lasts only through honest work.
